title: Human Metapneumovirus–associated Infections Among American Indian and Alaska Native Children, 2019–2024
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications. METHODS: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta). Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors. RESULTS: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In 2023-2024, incidence rates of HMPV-associated ARI hospitalization per 1000 children <5 years old were 11.3 (95% confidence interval: 8.6-14.8) in the Southwest, 10.3 (7.4-14.4) in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, and 0 (0-1.1) in Anchorage. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the lack of data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children. Active ARI surveillance was conducted among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children under 5 years of age in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska from November 2019 to May 2024. Data were collected via questionnaires and chart reviews, with nasal swabs tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens using polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates were calculated using Poisson regression, and seasonality and risk factors were assessed with multivariable modeling. Results showed that 13.0% of hospitalized children and 7.0% of outpatient children were HMPV-positive, with seasonality disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. Age <2 years and delayed care were significantly associated with increased risk of HMPV-associated hospitalization. The authors concluded that these findings serve as a baseline for future pediatric HMPV prevention strategies. The study's limitations include its focus on specific locations, which may limit generalizability, and its observational design, which may introduce confounding factors. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta).
analysis_en.methods: Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors.
analysis_en.main_results: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a baseline for understanding the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children, which can inform the development and implementation of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on specific tribal and geographic locations, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

title_zh: 与人偏肺病毒(人偏肺病毒)相关的美国原住民和阿拉斯加原住民儿童感染情况,2019-2024年
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications. METHODS: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta). Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors. RESULTS: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In 2023-2024, incidence rates of HMPV-associated ARI hospitalization per 1000 children <5 years old were 11.3 (95% confidence interval: 8.6-14.8) in the Southwest, 10.3 (7.4-14.4) in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, and 0 (0-1.1) in Anchorage. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.
abstract_zh: 背景:关于美国原住民/阿拉斯加原住民(AI/AN)儿童中与人偏肺病毒(HMPV)相关的急性呼吸道感染(ARI)的数据缺乏相关文献。方法:我们在纳瓦霍族地区、怀特山阿帕奇部落地区和阿拉斯加(安克雷奇和尤通凯斯克威姆河三角洲)的选定医疗机构中,对住院和门诊的<5岁AI/AN儿童进行了主动的ARI监测。从2019年11月至2024年5月,符合基于症状的ARI病例定义的儿童有资格参与研究。数据通过问卷和病历回顾收集。对中鼻甲鼻拭子进行聚合酶链反应检测HMPV和其他呼吸道病原体。使用泊松回归计算与HMPV相关的住院率。描述了季节性特征,并通过泊松多变量模型(稳健标准误差)评估了与HMPV相关住院的风险因素。结果:总体而言,13.0%(218/1683)的住院ARI儿童和7.0%(81/1165)的门诊ARI儿童检测出HMPV阳性。HMPV通常在12月至5月间流行;季节性和与HMPV相关的住院率在2019冠状病毒病大流行期间受到干扰。在2023-2024年,<5岁儿童中与HMPV相关的ARI住院率每1000人分别为西南地区11.3(95%置信区间:8.6-14.8)、尤通凯斯克威姆河三角洲10.3(7.4-14.4)和安克雷奇0(0-1.1)。在泊松模型中,年龄<2岁(调整风险比:1.43 [1.08-1.90])和发病后≥4天才就诊(1.38 [1.09-1.75])与HMPV相关的住院风险显著增加,与HMPV相关的门诊访问相比。结论:本分析记录了AI/AN<5岁儿童中与HMPV相关的ARI和住院负担,为未来儿童HMPV预防产品的使用提供了基础信息。

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating “late-small” and “early-large” epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

title: A one-step multiplex real-time reverse transcription quantitative PCR assay for rapid and simultaneous detection of human parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and rhinovirus in patients with acute respiratory tract infection
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Clinically, acute respiratory tract infections (ARIs) caused by human parainfluenza virus (PIV), human metapneumovirus (MPV), and human rhinoviruses (HRV) are often indistinguishable due to overlapping symptoms. This study aimed to develop a one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous, rapid, and accurate detection of PIV (types 1-4), MPV (subgroups A and B), and HRV (species A and B). METHODS: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV in clinical specimens. Primers and probes targeted conserved genomic regions, and an internal reference gene (B2M) was included for quality assurance. The limit of detection was determined via serial dilution of standard strains. Assay specificity was verified using 14 non-target pathogens, and repeatability was evaluated across various specimen concentrations. Clinical validation involved comparison with a commercial kit, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, agreement rate, and Kappa coefficient calculated for assessment. RESULTS: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was successfully developed for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV. The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, expressed as the equivalent concentration in the original specimen before nucleic acid extraction; this LOD was determined under multiplex co-amplification conditions, with all three targets present in the same reaction tube at every concentration level. No cross-reactivity was observed against the 14 specified non-target pathogens under the conditions evaluated, and all eight target strains were detected. Repeatability testing showed coefficients of variation (CV) of ≤ 2% for Ct values at low and medium concentrations. At the individual-target level, the sensitivity of the developed assay was 98.82% for HRV, 98.55% for PIV, and 100.0% for MPV, with specificity of 100.0% for all three targets. Pooled (target-level) sensitivity and specificity were 99.06% and 100.0%, respectively, and the overall agreement with the reference method was 99.24% (260/262). CONCLUSION: The method provides a technical approach for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV species A and B. Its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established.

title_zh: 一种一步法多重实时逆转录定量PCR检测方法用于快速同时检测急性呼吸道感染患者中的人副流感病毒、人偏肺病毒和鼻病毒
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Clinically, acute respiratory tract infections (ARIs) caused by human parainfluenza virus (PIV), human metapneumovirus (MPV), and human rhinoviruses (HRV) are often indistinguishable due to overlapping symptoms. This study aimed to develop a one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous, rapid, and accurate detection of PIV (types 1-4), MPV (subgroups A and B), and HRV (species A and B). METHODS: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV in clinical specimens. Primers and probes targeted conserved genomic regions, and an internal reference gene (B2M) was included for quality assurance. The limit of detection was determined via serial dilution of standard strains. Assay specificity was verified using 14 non-target pathogens, and repeatability was evaluated across various specimen concentrations. Clinical validation involved comparison with a commercial kit, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, agreement rate, and Kappa coefficient calculated for assessment. RESULTS: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was successfully developed for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV. The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, expressed as the equivalent concentration in the original specimen before nucleic acid extraction; this LOD was determined under multiplex co-amplification conditions, with all three targets present in the same reaction tube at every concentration level. No cross-reactivity was observed against the 14 specified non-target pathogens under the conditions evaluated, and all eight target strains were detected. Repeatability testing showed coefficients of variation (CV) of ≤ 2% for Ct values at low and medium concentrations. At the individual-target level, the sensitivity of the developed assay was 98.82% for HRV, 98.55% for PIV, and 100.0% for MPV, with specificity of 100.0% for all three targets. Pooled (target-level) sensitivity and specificity were 99.06% and 100.0%, respectively, and the overall agreement with the reference method was 99.24% (260/262). CONCLUSION: The method provides a technical approach for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV species A and B. Its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established.
abstract_zh: 目的:临床中,由人副流感病毒(PIV)、人偏肺病毒(MPV)和人鼻病毒(HRV)引起的急性呼吸道感染(ARIs)由于症状重叠而常常难以区分。本研究旨在开发一种一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法,用于同时、快速且准确地检测PIV(1-4型)、MPV(A和B亚组)以及HRV(A和B种)。方法:建立了一种一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法,用于临床样本中PIV、MPV和HRV的同时检测。引物和探针针对保守的基因组区域,且包含一个内部参考基因(B2M)以确保检测质量。通过标准菌株的连续稀释确定检测限。使用14种非目标病原体验证检测特异性,并在不同样本浓度下评估重复性。临床验证通过与商业试剂盒进行比较,计算敏感性、特异性、预测值、符合率和Kappa系数以进行评估。结果:成功开发了一种用于同时检测PIV、MPV和HRV的一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法。该检测方法对所有三个目标的检测限为100 copies/mL,以核酸提取前原始样本的等效浓度表示;该检测限是在多重共扩增条件下确定的,所有三个目标在每个浓度水平下均存在于同一反应管中。在评估条件下,未观察到对14种指定非目标病原体的交叉反应,并检测到了所有8种目标菌株。重复性测试显示,在低和中等浓度下,Ct值的变异系数(CV)≤2%。在单个目标水平上,所开发检测方法的敏感性分别为HRV 98.82%、PIV 98.55%和MPV 100.0%,特异性均为100.0%。合并(目标水平)的敏感性和特异性分别为99.06%和100.0%,与参考方法的总体符合率为99.24%(260/262)。结论:该方法为同时检测PIV、MPV和HRV A、B种提供了一种技术途径。其相对于全面呼吸道病原体检测面板的临床实用性仍有待确立。

title: A Study to Assess the Effectiveness of Planned Teaching Programme on Knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among Parents of School Going Children Age Group of 6-12 Years in Selected Community Area: A Pre-Experimental
abstract: Human metapneumovirus is a negative-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the family Pneumoviridae and is closely related to the avian metapneumovirus subgroup C. Globally In 2018, there were an estimated 14.2 million acute lower respiratory infection cases associated with human metapneumovirus in children under 5 years old. In one study, 113 out of 4519 samples tested were positive for human metapneumovirus. Human metapneumovirus is a major global cause of respiratory infections with an overall pooled prevalence of about 5.3% among patients with respiratory illness and a higher prevalence of 5-25% in children. Objectives: To assess the knowledge of parents of school going children's age group of 6-12 years regarding Human Metapneumovirus selected community area, to assess the effectiveness of Planned Teaching Programme on knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school going children age group of 6-12 years in selected community area, to determine the association between knowledge levels and selected demographic variables regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school going children age group of 6-12 years in selected community area. Materials and Methods: A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test resign design were used. 100 parents of school going children participated in this study. The sample size was calculated by using Cochran's sample size formula. Quantitative research design was used. Non-Probability convenient sampling technique was used to select the sample. The data were collected from selected community area, using socio demographic data sheet and structured knowledge questionnaires. Consent was obtained from participant in the study. Results: In this study, majority of the subjects 28% were from the age group of 10-11 years and 12 years, majority of the subjects 55% were female, majority of the subjects 66% were belongs to Hindu religion, majority of the subjects 40% were study up to secondary education, majority of the subjects 28% were work as a housewife and majority of the subjects 55% having no any knowledge about human metapneumovirus. In pre-test, majority 59% of subjects had average level of knowledge score, 36% had good level of knowledge score, 4% had poor level of knowledge score, 1% had very good level of knowledge score and 0% had excellent level of knowledge score. Mean knowledge score in pre-test of the subjects was 11.65 + 2.931. Minimum knowledge score in pre-test was 04 and maximum knowledge score in pre-test was 21. While in post-test, majority 57% of subjects had good level of knowledge score, 27% had very good level of knowledge score, 16% had average level of knowledge score and 0% had poor and excellent level of knowledge score. Mean knowledge score in post-test of the subjects was 16.36 + 3.267. Minimum knowledge score in post-test was 09 and maximum knowledge score in post-test was 22. Conclusion: The written prepared material by the investigator in the form of planned teaching helped the subject to improve their knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school-going children. The study also found no significant association between post-test knowledge scores and most demographic variables, except for the education of parents, which showed a significant influence. The planned teaching programme proved to be an effective method for enhancing parental knowledge on Human Metapneumovirus.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

title: Sendai virus, a candidate vaccine for the prevention of respiratory virus infections in children: a review
abstract: Background Respiratory viruses including human parainfluenza virus (hPIV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), pose serious, potentially lethal threats to humans, particularly infants and young children. While maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies are advancing to provide transient protection against these viruses, licensed pediatric vaccines are not yet available. Sendai virus (SeV) is now being developed as an intranasal (I.N.) vaccine candidate for the prevention of serious respiratory viral infections in children. Methods To examine the potential of replication-competent Sendai virus and its recombinants as pediatric respiratory virus vaccines against hPIV, RSV and hMPV, we searched literature databases and evaluated both historical and contemporary published research. Results SeV and SeV recombinant vaccines have been tested pre-clinically in a variety of animal models and in Phase I clinical studies. In pre-clinical models, a single dose of SeV induced rapid and long-lasting B- and T-cell responses in the upper respiratory tract and blood. When recombinant SeV constructs were produced and formulated into cocktail vaccines, they were protective against four different respiratory pathogens simultaneously. Vaccines were successful when partnered with passively transferred antibodies; specifically, when a recombinant SeV-based RSV vaccine was tested in the presence of passively transferred monoclonal or polyclonal PIV-specific or RSV-specific antibodies in a cotton rat model, the vaccine provided durable protective immunity against RSV. In clinical trials, SeV was well-tolerated and uniformly immunogenic in PIV-seropositive 1–2 year old children. Methods have been developed for the manufacture of stable SeV-based vaccine products, compatible with wide global distribution of SeV vaccines for clinical use. Conclusion To date, results highlight SeV as an attractive pediatric vaccine candidate. Continued clinical testing of SeV may provide global relief from serious respiratory viral infections in infants and young children.

abstract_zh: 背景 人副流感病毒(hPIV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV)等呼吸道病毒对人类构成严重且可能致命的威胁,尤其是对婴儿和幼儿。尽管母源性抗病毒药物和单克隆抗体正在推进以提供对这些病毒的暂时保护,但目前尚未有获批用于儿科的抗病毒药物。副流感病毒(SeV)现在正被开发为一种鼻内给药(I.N.)的候选疫苗,用于预防儿童严重的呼吸道病毒感染。方法 为了评估复制型副流感病毒及其重组体作为针对hPIV、RSV和hMPV的儿科呼吸道病毒疫苗的潜力,我们搜索了文献数据库并评估了历史和现代发表的研究。结果 SeV及其重组体疫苗已在多种动物模型和一期临床研究中进行了临床前测试。在临床前模型中,单次剂量的SeV在上呼吸道和血液中诱导了快速且持久的B细胞和T细胞免疫应答。当重组SeV构建体被制备并配制成混合疫苗时,它们能够同时对四种不同的呼吸道病原体提供保护。当重组SeV为基础的RSV疫苗与被动转移的抗体联合使用时,其在棉花鼠模型中显示出持久的保护性免疫。在临床试验中,SeV在PIV抗体阳性的1-2岁儿童中耐受性良好且具有统一的免疫原性。已经开发出制造稳定SeV为基础的疫苗产品的工艺,使其适用于全球范围内的临床使用。结论 目前的结果突显了SeV作为儿科疫苗候选者的吸引力。持续的临床试验可能为婴儿和幼儿严重的呼吸道病毒感染提供全球性的缓解。

title: Temporal dynamics of respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients in Shanghai, 2019–2023: a multi-center longitudinal surveillance study
abstract: COVID-19 greatly reshaped the epidemiology of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.This study explored temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic. A retrospective multi-center observational study was performed across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China (2019–2023). Hospitalized SARI patients aged ≥ 15 years were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). We stratified the study period into pre-pandemic (2019), pandemic (2020–2022), and post-pandemic (2023) phases for comparative analysis. In total, 4738 participants were enrolled. The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) ( P <0.001). A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established: (1) decline-resurgence for influenza virus (IFV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ), Bordetella pertussis ( B. pertussis ), and human bocavirus (HBoV); (2) sustained decline for human parainfluenza virus (HPIV), human coronavirus (HCoV), human adenovirus (HAdV), human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV), and Legionella pneumophila ( L. pneumophila ); (3) transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV); (4) continuous increase for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). IFV, HRV/EV, and HCoV consistently ranked top five across all periods. pneumoniae was the dominant pathogen (33.65%) in patients aged 15–44 years. Seasonal peaks of IFV and RSV were substantially reshaped in the post-pandemic period. The co-infection rate was 1.14% (54/4738), with IFV- M. pneumoniae was the most combination (20.37%). Respiratory pathogen circulation patterns changed substantially from 2019 to 2023. Persistent multi-pathogen surveillance is required to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective multi-center observational study was conducted across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China, from 2019 to 2023, enrolling a total of 4738 participants aged ≥ 15 years.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established, including a transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV).

The findings highlight the need for persistent multi-pathogen surveillance to monitor shifts in pathogen circulation and prevent outbreaks. The study's design, while observational, is supported by a large sample size and comprehensive testing, providing moderate confidence in its conclusions.

title_zh: 2019–2023年上海成人严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)患者呼吸道病原体的时间动态变化:一项多中心纵向监测研究
source_body_en: COVID-19 greatly reshaped the epidemiology of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.This study explored temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic. A retrospective multi-center observational study was performed across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China (2019–2023). Hospitalized SARI patients aged ≥ 15 years were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). We stratified the study period into pre-pandemic (2019), pandemic (2020–2022), and post-pandemic (2023) phases for comparative analysis. In total, 4738 participants were enrolled. The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) ( P <0.001). A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established: (1) decline-resurgence for influenza virus (IFV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ), Bordetella pertussis ( B. pertussis ), and human bocavirus (HBoV); (2) sustained decline for human parainfluenza virus (HPIV), human coronavirus (HCoV), human adenovirus (HAdV), human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV), and Legionella pneumophila ( L. pneumophila ); (3) transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV); (4) continuous increase for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). IFV, HRV/EV, and HCoV consistently ranked top five across all periods. pneumoniae was the dominant pathogen (33.65%) in patients aged 15–44 years. Seasonal peaks of IFV and RSV were substantially reshaped in the post-pandemic period. The co-infection rate was 1.14% (54/4738), with IFV- M. pneumoniae was the most combination (20.37%). Respiratory pathogen circulation patterns changed substantially from 2019 to 2023. Persistent multi-pathogen surveillance is required to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics.

title: Beyond Croup: A Phenotype-Based Perspective on Parainfluenza Virus Types in Children
abstract: Human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) caused an estimated 18.8 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 725 000 hospitalizations, and 34 400 deaths among children under 5 in 2018, ranking second only to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection and disease in children. It examines the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of hMPV, emphasizing the need for targeted strategies in pediatric care.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic review methods or meta-analysis. It provides general background on hMPV and its clinical relevance without detailing specific databases or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that hMPV infections are distinct from other parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) in terms of epidemiology, clinical syndrome, and immune response. It highlights the importance of recognizing these differences for improved clinical management and the development of targeted interventions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that hMPV has historically been underrecognized due to limitations in diagnostic methods. It also identifies gaps in understanding the full spectrum of hMPV-related diseases and the need for more robust data on its impact in different populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that advances in molecular diagnostics are critical for accurate identification of hMPV infections. It also emphasizes the need for further research into hMPV-specific therapeutics and vaccines, as well as improved surveillance and clinical management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in children, emphasizing the need for targeted strategies in pediatric care. It notes that hMPV has historically been underrecognized due to diagnostic limitations and underscores the importance of improved surveillance and research into hMPV-specific interventions. The review also identifies gaps in understanding the full spectrum of hMPV-related diseases and calls for further investigation into its impact in different populations.

title: Cost-effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines in post-marketing settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, particularly among infants and older adults worldwide. This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines. METHODS: In this review, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 20, 2025. Grey literature and reference lists were also searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for older adults and infants. Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions. RESULTS: Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval (CI): USD 41.89-168.21; I2 = 93.2%]. For infants, the pooled INB was USD 5.81 (95% CI: USD - 35.44-47.07; I2 = 89.4%). In the European subgroup, the pooled INB among older adults was USD 123.63 (95% CI: USD 41.23-206.02; I2 = 89.4%), while that for infants was USD 15.00 (95% CI: USD - 4.33-34.34; I2 = 43.4%). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses showed robust pooled INBs among older adults, whereas infant estimates were sensitive to study exclusion. CONCLUSIONS: At the thresholds used in the included studies, RSV vaccination might be cost-effective for older adults in post-marketing settings, while the evidence for maternal vaccination remained inconclusive. Descriptive findings suggested that age- and risk-based targeting in older adults and seasonal maternal vaccination may yield higher INB estimates. Substantial between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates and highlights the need to consider local epidemiology and implementation conditions when developing RSV vaccination policies.

title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.
abstract: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30-60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

title: Incidence, shedding, and transmission of common respiratory viruses: data from a prospective, longitudinal, household cohort study in the Gambia from March 2021-June 2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings. We aimed to compare the epidemiology of multiple respiratory viruses within households in the Gambia. METHODS: We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year. Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables. FINDINGS: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03). We found evidence for reductions in incidence risk with increasing age for HRV, RSV, seasonal coronaviruses, and parainfluenza viruses, with no difference for SARS-CoV-2. Among 719 index infections, the mean household SARs for all viruses combined was 6.7%. Infection with prolonged shedding (p = 0.002), specific viral species (p < 0.0001) and a lower Ct value were associated with increased transmission. INTERPRETATION: A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species. FUNDING: This study was funded through a UK Research and Innovation grant.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒是低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)发病率的主要原因之一,但在社区环境中对其传播、风险因素和感染动态了解甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们在冈比亚的一个郊区地区开展了一项前瞻性家庭研究。纳入了至少有5名成员、包括至少一名成人和一名儿童的家庭,并进行了为期一年的随访。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在家庭中,呼吸道病毒的传播主要由大量无症状感染驱动,不同病毒种类在传播、排毒和持续性方面存在关键差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为社区环境中呼吸道病毒的防控策略和风险评估提供依据,特别是强调无症状感染在家庭传播中的作用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅在冈比亚的一个郊区地区进行,限制了其普遍适用性。由于样本量大且数据收集全面,证据强度较强。

title: Vaccine profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in adults: prevention of RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and emerging evidence of potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and hospitalization in older adults, individuals with certain chronic medical conditions, and immunocompromised patients. RSV can result in acute and longer-term cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity, and declines in physical functioning and quality of life. AREAS COVERED: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 was the first RSV vaccine licensed for preventing RSV-LRTD in adults, with initial approvals in 2023 in the United States and Europe. Robust clinical trial data showed an acceptable safety profile and demonstrated efficacy against RSV-LRTD, with exploratory post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in RSV-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)/asthma exacerbations. These findings are reinforced by real-world evidence showing effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations, COPD/asthma exacerbations, and cardiovascular events. EXPERT OPINION: This emerging evidence supports a broader role of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 beyond preventing RSV-LRTD alone to preserve cardiovascular and respiratory health. RSV vaccination should be considered within an integrated routine care and preventive management strategy for older adults and individuals with chronic conditions, alongside other adult immunizations and health interventions. Addressing implementation barriers for adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and emphasizing its role in maintaining health and independence will be critical to enable widespread uptake and help protect patient health.

title: Hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of respiratory viral infections in Spain: A population-based study using hospital data (2019-2023).
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory viral infections are a major cause of hospitalization, morbidity, mortality, and healthcare resource use in Spain. Although influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for most of the healthcare burden, the contribution of other respiratory viruses has been less studied. This study aimed to analyze the hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of these infections during the 2019-2023 period. METHODS: A retrospective population-based study was conducted using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (CMBD), including hospitalizations with a diagnosis of respiratory viral infection between 2019 and 2023. Influenza, RSV, adenovirus, metapneumovirus, parainfluenza, and rhinovirus were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 154,753 hospitalizations were included (mean age: 39 years; 48.6% female). Influenza and RSV accounted for most hospitalizations and total costs. A marked reduction in hospitalizations was observed in 2021, followed by recovery in 2022-2023. RSV, metapneumovirus, rhinovirus, and adenovirus predominantly affected the pediatric population, whereas influenza and parainfluenza had a greater impact on older adults. Overall, 6.5% of patients required ICU admission and in-hospital mortality was 2.7%, highest for influenza (4.2%). Metapneumovirus and rhinovirus showed the highest ICU admission rates. Mean hospital stay was 6.1 days (7.4 days in ICU). Although influenza and RSV generated the highest total costs, other viruses showed higher costs per episode. CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory viral infections impose a substantial healthcare and economic burden, with variable impact according to virus type and age group, highlighting the need for integrated surveillance, prevention, and healthcare planning strategies.

title: Human bocavirus infection among hospitalized children in eastern China: epidemiology, co-infection, and time-series forecasting
abstract: Background Acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) are the leading cause of pediatric hospitalization worldwide; data on human bocavirus (HBoV) epidemiology in eastern China remain scarce. Methods We enrolled 12,630 hospitalized children <18 years with ARTI from January 2025 to March 2026 across tertiary hospitals in eastern China. HBoV and other respiratory pathogens were detected using a commercial 13-target multiplex RT-PCR panel (SureX 13 Respiratory Pathogen Multiplex Kit; Ningbo Health Gene Technologies). A SARIMA model forecast HBoV positive rates for the next 30 weeks. Results Overall HBoV positive rate was 3.2%, with no sex difference ( p = 0.99) but peaking in children aged 1–<3 years (7.7%) and during June–October. Most common co-infections were human rhinovirus (Rhv), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human parainfluenza viruses (HPIV). Length of stay did not differ significantly across co-infection groups; the longest mean stay ( Mycoplasma pneumoniae , 8.3 days) was not significantly longer than the shortest (Chlamydia, 4.0 days; p = 0.279). By infection multiplicity, 230 children had mono-infection, 154 double infection, and 26 triple infection; mean length of stay was 5.9, 6.1, and 6.7 days, respectively (one-way ANOVA, F = 0.357, p = 0.700). Mean outcome score was lowest for triple infection (0.982) and highest for mono-infection (1.014). The SARIMA model predicts HBoV peaks in August and September 2026. Conclusion HBoV infection in hospitalized children in eastern China shows clear age (1–3 years) and seasonal (summer–autumn) patterns with frequent co-infections; specific combinations, notably HBoV–ADV double infection and the triple-infection subgroup ( n = 26), showed descriptively poorer outcomes but no statistically significant differences, warranting confirmation in larger cohorts. These findings support targeted diagnosis, prevention, and resource planning.

title: Immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain and efforts to shield it
abstract: Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO®, subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain. To dampen Foldon-induced antibody responses, we engineered influenza computationally optimized broadly reactive antigen (COBRA) HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three different sites in Foldon. Mass spectrometry analyses confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of the three intended sites. Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens demonstrated reduced binding by anti-Foldon monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies compared to the wild-type COBRA HA Foldon. However, mice immunized with the COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens did not have a significant reduction in the elicitation of anti-Foldon antibodies. Further analysis suggested that some of the observed differences in antibody binding to mutant Foldon antigens can be attributed to differences in protein sequence alone. Altogether, these data suggest that while the N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon from reactive antibodies, this shielding does not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. Importantly, these data highlight that the Foldon trimerization domain is immunogenic, which should be considered during clinical trials of vaccines that contain Foldon.

title: Epidemiological characteristics of 11 respiratory pathogens among 19,382 hospitalized children in Putian city
abstract: Objective To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of common respiratory pathogens among children hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Putian city with the aim of providing a scientific basis for regional pediatric respiratory infection prevention. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on clinical data from 19,382 children hospitalized at the Affiliated Hospital of Putian University between January 1, 2023, and December 30, 2025. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) combined with capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis was employed to detect 11 common respiratory pathogens. Results A total of 19,382 hospitalized children were enrolled, with an overall respiratory pathogen positivity rate of 69.40%. The positivity rate was highest among preschool-aged children and lowest among adolescents. Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) exhibited the highest detection rate in school-aged children (38.57%), while human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) demonstrated the highest detection rate in infants and toddlers (19.53%). The pathogen positivity rate was 70.24% in males and 68.20% in females, with a statistically significant difference between sexes. Among the 19,382 children with ARTIs, single-pathogen detection predominated, accounting for 58.89%; dual-pathogen detection accounted for 9.93%, and multiple-pathogen detection accounted for 0.57%. Respiratory pathogen positivity rates showed seasonal fluctuations, peaking in winter 2023 (73.98%), spring 2024 (77.85%), and autumn 2025 (74.17%). In addition, the positivity rates of influenza A virus (InfA), influenza B virus (InfB) decreased with increasing temperature, whereas those of HRSV, human coronavirus (HCOV) increased with increasing temperature. A total of 15,601 pathogen detection events were recorded; the three most frequently detected pathogens were human rhinovirus (HRV; 24.66%), Mp (23.68%), and HRSV (14.52%). Conclusion The overall positivity rate of respiratory pathogens among children hospitalized with ARTIs in Putian was high (69.40%), with distinct age-related and seasonal characteristics. Mp predominated in school-aged children, whereas HRSV predominated in infants and toddlers. Pathogen detection peaked in autumn–winter 2023, spring 2024, and autumn 2025. HRV, Mp, and HRSV were the three dominant pathogens. The dual- and multiple-detection groups had median hospital stays of 6 days, compared with 5 days in the pathogen-negative and single-detection groups. These findings provide a scientific basis for optimizing clinical diagnosis and treatment of pediatric respiratory infections in this region.
